cells.raw_text: Moderate goal-directed fluid resuscitation, low-dose vasopressors
Judicious fluid resuscitation, positional preload reduction, vasopressor + inotrope
Global hypokinesis, thrombus stability, biventricular function
Strict volume restriction, positional preload reduction, low-dose vasopressors
None (no coronary artery disease, hypertension, diabetes, prior surgery, or allergies)
Right lower limb redness, swelling, exudation for 1 day
BP 82/46 mmHg (MAP 58 mmHg), HR 150 bpm (atrial flutter), RR 28/min, temperature 38.9 °C, SpO_(2) 92% (FiO_(2) 0.5)
Pro-BNP 12,140.5 pg/mL, high-sensitivity troponin T elevated, CRP 214.0 mg/L, lactate 4.6 mmol/L
LVEF 16%, four-chamber enlargement, left ventricular apical thrombus (29 × 25 mm)
Right great saphenous vein thrombosis, acute kidney injury, hypoalbuminemia
6VT-D TEE probe (compatible with Vivid E95 or E90 ultrasound system)
2D, M-mode, color doppler, pulse-wave doppler, continuous-wave doppler, 3D/4D (Live 3D TEE)
Tip dimensions: 15.2 mm × 10.5 mm × 8.2 mm; shaft length: 110 cm; bending section: two-way (anterior/posterior) 120°, lateral 90°
High-level disinfection with peracetic acid (e.g., Cidex OPA)
Real-time LVEF, regional wall motion, cavity dimensions
LV and RV size/function, thrombus stability (apical), biventricular interaction
Orthogonal LVEF assessment, anterior/inferior wall motion
LVOT patency, aortic valve morphology, thrombus extension
Volume status (IVC collapsibility; < 15% indicated adequate preload)
Repeat TTE at Day 5: LVEF 22%, thrombus stable

Right lower limb necrotizing fasciitis; rapidly progressed to septic shock; intubation and mechanical ventilation; initial resuscitation; TTE showed severe dilated cardiomyopathy (LVEF 16%) and left ventricular apical thrombus; elevated Pro-BNP, troponin, lactate, CRP and procalcitonin; broad-spectrum antibiotics initiated; CRRT for acute kidney injury
Hemodynamic stabilization with norepinephrine, dobutamine, amiodarone and esmolol; lactate decreased to 3.1 mmol/L; ongoing infection control and anticoagulation

Emergency debridement under TEE-guided anesthesia; cardiac-sparing induction; strict fluid restriction; 20° head-up tilt; TEE monitoring of biventricular function, thrombus stability and volume status; targeted vasoactive drug titration; lactate normalized to 1.7 mmol/L; hemodynamically stable

ICU admission; continued inotropic and vasopressor support; CRRT-guided negative fluid balance; gradual weaning of vasoactive agents; improved wound healing; TTE on Day 5 revealed LVEF 22% with stable thrombus
Patient discharged home in stable condition without major adverse cardiac events
MCS, mechanical circulatory support; IVC, inferior vena cava; CO, cardiac output; SV, stroke volume.

MAP, mean arterial pressure; HR, heart rate; NE, norepinephrine; DB, dobutamine; ES, esmolol; AM, amiodarone; TEE, transesophageal echocardiography; ICU, intensive care unit; LVEF, left ventricular ejection fraction; LV thrombus, left ventricular thrombus; CRRT, continuous renal replacement therapy.
All views were obtained with care to avoid excessive probe manipulation given the presence of left ventricular thrombus.

limitations: Only the serial perioperative table (Table 5) is a series; single-value baseline cells (age, body mass index in Table 2) are not serial and were left unused.
Table 5 MAP, heart rate and most vasoactive drug cells are printed ranges or text and parse as unparseable; they are kept as raw cells without numeric conversion.
Row labels (Day 1, Day 2, postoperative day) use different anchors and the Day numbering does not match the March 8 surgery date, so no offsets were entered.
The machine draft heuristic headers were not used; series were rebuilt column-wise and each time cell was checked by hand against its row label.
